newsitem.title: MEXICO: FOCUS-NBC, Mexico's Azteca in legal battle.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-NBC, Mexico's Azteca in legal battle.

text.p: Mexico's Number Two television network TV Azteca said on Wednesday it plans to block efforts by the U.S. National Broadcasting Co (NBC) network to buy a stake in the Mexican firm.

Both sides will take the dispute to the International Chamber of Commerce in Paris to decide which side failed to live up to a joint venture agreement signed in May 1994 that gave NBC a right to buy up to 20 percent of Azteca.
"Simply put, things we were promised by NBC were not delivered," an official at Azteca, who did not want to be identified, told Reuters.

NBC officials, in turn, accused the Mexican network of "playing dirty" and said NBC was confident it would win the arbitration. Sources close to NBC told Reuters the company could seek as much as $27.5 million from Azteca in court.
In the deal, NBC agreed to license shows to Azteca, to allow the Mexican firm to use the NBC logo and to provide a host of consulting services in marketing, sales and programming.

In return, Azteca promised to pay NBC $7 million and granted it the rights to buy up to 10 percent of the Mexican network before May 1997 and an additional 10 percent if and when Azteca, a privately held firm, decided to go public.

NBC, a unit of General Electric Co, now wants to buy one percent of Azteca and retain the right to purchase another 10 percent in a public offering, the company said in a statement released in Mexico City on Tuesday.
But Azteca said in a statement that NBC failed to provide the help it promised, and added it would seek financial compensation from the U.S. network. It said it uses no NBC programming currently.
"...(The help) did not happen, and although Azteca needed help on several occasions, what it received was far from what had been agreed upon by both parties," it added.
NBC spokesman George Jamison told Reuters on Wednesday that NBC in past years was key in helping the upstart Azteca gain market share against its powerful rival Grupo Televisa SA .

Jamison said Azteca still owes NBC some $5 million from the original agreement. And sources close to NBC said the company also wants some $22.5 million from Azteca as payment for warrants in the original pact that NBC did not exercise.

A former state-owned network, Azteca has been a success story since it was privatized in 1993 by former President Carlos Salinas, steadily wooing viewers from media giant Televisa and generating profits.
Since the joint venture was signed, Azteca has doubled its market share from roughly 12 percent to about 25 percent, according to independent estimates.

In a recent interview with Reuters, Azteca head Ricardo Salinas Pliego, who also owns Mexican retailer Grupo Elektra , said he had no plans to take the fast-growing company public for another three to four years.

Salinas Pliego is no relation to the former Mexican president, but does have a business link to the former president's brother Raul, who is in jail on charges of murder, corruption and money laundering.
Salinas Pliego caused a scandal late last year when he admitted he took $30 million in loans from Raul Salinas shortly before the Azteca sale.
